description_long: The Associated Press reconstructed the hours before Trump ordered Operation Epic Fury against Iran. At 12:25 p.m. on February 27, 2026, Trump told reporters he was unhappy with indirect nuclear negotiations and had not made a final decision. At 3:38 p.m., while flying aboard Air Force One, he ordered the operation, according to a timeline Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine later presented. AP reported that Trump asked Republican lawmakers on the flight to discuss the choice between continuing talks and striking; the report attributed the account to a person with direct knowledge. Oman’s foreign minister Badr Albusaidi later said an agreement had been within reach and expressed dismay that the negotiations were undermined. Together, these details establish a sequence of public remarks, a private discussion with lawmakers, a military order and a mediator’s view of the talks. The timeline does not show that Trump deliberately cultivated ambiguity to preserve deniability, make escalation easier, or make diplomacy politically untenable. Those claims about motive and effect go beyond the chronology.
